latest.summary: # Tenstorrent hits $6.2B valuation to scale open-weight AI chips. Tenstorrent, a chip startup focused on inference, has raised $1.5 billion at a $6.2 billion valuation. The round comes five months aft...
highlights: # Tenstorrent hits $6.2B valuation to scale open-weight AI chips. Tenstorrent, a chip startup focused on inference, has raised $1.5 billion at a $6.2 billion valuation. The round comes five months after the 10-year-old Nvidia challenger reportedly received acquisition interest from Intel and Qualcomm at valuations of as much as $5 billion. The fresh round, which more than doubled Tenstorrent’s valuation from the $2.6 billion it fetched in late 2024, was led by Trace Capital, a new firm launched by Quiet Capital co-founder Ben Mahdavi, and Innovation X. The new capital will go toward scaling chips tailored for serving open-weight AI models and video generation. Tenstorrent is part of a wave of AI hardware startups trying to chip away at Nvidia’s dominance. Among them is Etched, an AI chip maker that was fielding investment offers at valuations of $40 billion or more, TechCrunch reported earlier this month. latest.title: Amazon is taking its biggest shot at Nvidia yet with new TorchNeuron dev tool - TechCrunch
latest.summary: On Monday, Amazon Web Services released a tool called TorchNeuron that lets AI startups easily move their AI apps onto Amazon’s AI chip, Trainium. In doing so, Amazon is also taking a direct stab at t...
highlights: On Monday, Amazon Web Services released a tool called TorchNeuron that lets AI startups easily move their AI apps onto Amazon’s AI chip, Trainium. In doing so, Amazon is also taking a direct stab at the the software advantage that has helped Nvidia become the default hardware choice for AI apps, and spurred its rise as AI hardware provider of choice. TorchNeuron works with PyTorch, a free, open-source toolkit that developers use to build, train, and run AI models. It lets AI apps written with PyTorch run on Trainium by changing just one line of configuration, according to Amazon — no code rewrite required. Nvidia has spent years ensuring its CUDA software — the software infrastructure that allows apps to run on Nvidia GPUs and its other hardware — seamlessly supports AI apps written with PyTorch. However, Amazon argues that porting to Trainium isn’t just easy; it also gives AI startups access to Amazon’s entire cloud.

The AI offering enables scaled AI deployment across industrial enterprises, according to the firm, and is set to reduce new product introduction timelines by 25%.***. And Tata Consultancy Services’ intelligence foundry is aiming to address the critical gap between AI experimentation and enterprise-wide execution, providing industry-specific agents which can integrate into existing workflows safely and securely. Speaking on the opportunity, Ramachandran S, practice leader for engineering and manufacturing in HFS Research, said, “Most enterprise AI still lives on desktops, while there is untapped value on shop floors in industrial and physical AI. Industrial Intelligence Foundry is TCS’ bet to fill this gap with domain-specific AI, with the potential for significant business impact, scaling AI Implementations and not just another agentic AI project.”. According to a statement from the firm, the offering can “help enterprises reduce new product introduction timelines by 25% and improve manufacturing productivity by 20-25%”.
